title: Europe's Digital Future: How to Get from User to Shaper?

segments.text: Hello and welcome back. I'm now very
excited to have somebody from the
government here and it's Karsten Vilmar
Germany's Minister of Digital
Transformation and Government
Modernization.
He's going to talk to us for about 10
minutes about Europe's digital future,
how to get from user to shaper and then
I'm very excited as well to get like
Larissa Holtzki up here from
Handelsblatt. She's the editorial head
of the tech edition there and she's
going to interview him about what he
talked about and what else we can learn
from that. I think it's incredibly
important that the politics and
governments are actually part of what we
do here. I think software has always
been political thing and it's great to
have people that actually want to shape
the future. So please give a big hand
for Mr. Karsten Vilmar.
>> [music]
[music]
>> Good morning everyone.
And it's a real pleasure to be here at
the We Are Developers World Congress
Europe in Berlin.
And when I look around in this hall,
very hard to see with this light, but
I see much more than IT experts. I see
potentially also the architects of
Europe's digital future.
And that is why I also gladly took
on the patronage patronage of this world
congress.
And this is not just a formality for me.
It's a commitment.
We do not need you as spectators.
We need you as creators, as builders.
And Europe's digital future is not
written by politics. It's written where
developers, industry and policy makers
step up together.
And let me share with you one one
thought. I actually cannot imagine a
better time to be courageous,
to be a founder, to be developer than
today.
Some may say
not just given all the crisis we have,
is that really true
when AI is changing the role of
developers so profoundly?
And my answer is yes.
Yes, AI will change the way developers
work.
But it also makes great developers even
more powerful.
And those who understand this
technology, embrace it, and use it well,
will be able
to my multiply their own capacity
in ways we have never seen before.
And that is why this is such an
extraordinary moment
to have the courage
to do something big, to start eventually
your own company, to make a difference,
to use a technology that multiplies what
a single person was used to be able to
do.
And to build all of this, we need
developers, we need you.
And
this is my message to you today. And I
will also become a bit more specific and
concrete, but dream big and go for it.
Building something is never a straight
line.
Maybe it doesn't work the first time.
So you try a second time and a third
time. And maybe on the fourth attempt it
works and it becomes big. And that is
not failure. That is the path.
You get back up, you dust yourself off,
you take what you've learned and you try
again.
And every great company
started as an idea
that someone was brave enough to chase.
So have the courage to think big, to
challenge the status quo,
to eventually build the companies others
said was impossible.
And I believe
no generation have more reasons to be
bold than yours right now. And let me
explain
what I mean.
I know we have many crises,
many challenges right now. And there are
many reasons to be worried and
concerned.
But I tell you also, even though when
it's not totally visible, something is
happening in this country at the moment
as well. For a long time, Germany was
cautious. We watched deep tech,
great technology shifts from the side.
We were slow, we over-regulated, we bet
on the comfortable and the known instead
of the new. And that is changing right
now.
And transformation means one thing,
changing the status quo.
And in transformation, only one thing
matters, the rate of change.
Not where you stand,
but how fast you move.
And we are cutting bureaucracy,
we are serious about becoming more
independent. We are betting on growth
and on deep tech, exactly the things we
neglected for too long.
And you can see it in the numbers.
In the first half of this year, more
than 3,000 startups were founded in
Germany.
That is almost as many as during the
entire year before,
which was
the year on record ever.
And roughly one in three of them is
built on the basis of AI.
On top of that, seven new German
unicorns, seven billion-dollar companies
in the first half of this year alone, in
robotics, in energy,
in defense, in software. And that is not
a coincidence. That is momentum we have
to accelerate.
And that is the way you change the
status quo, you accelerate.
And this is the message I want to bring
to you today. Germany is moving.
So, I encourage you to move with us.
And
there is a big why it matters. There has
never been a better moment because the
stakes have never been higher.
A few weeks ago,
thousands of engineers in Europe sat
down to work and found the door locked.
Access to one of the world's
most powerful AI models switched off
overnight. No vote,
no warning.
And whatever one thinks of that
decision, it makes one thing clear.
This is no longer an abstract debate.
Access can change overnight.
Dependencies can become visible
overnight.
And sovereignty means we can still act
if things like that happen.
And sovereignty means we actively
compete and build products and solutions
here in Germany and here in Europe.
And I say it clearly, Europe is not
short of talent. We have world-class
research. We have deep industry
expertise. We have strong small and
medium-sized enterprises,
entrepreneurial energy,
and we have the rule of law, and we have
values.
But that is not enough. The next phase
will belong to those who master the
technology and to embed it where it
matters most, in industry, in public
administration, in critical
infrastructure, and in democratic life.
Europe has real strength, but strength
only becomes power when we turn it into
speed, scale, and trust. And the current
development of AI calls for the most
decisive political agenda and action
since the Second World War.
And sovereignty, let me be also clear,
is not isolation. It's not solitude.
It is the ability to choose. It's the
ability to compete and to grow. And
obviously, we still cherish trusted
partnerships,
but we also have to find and courage to
build products ourselves.
And this all is not a limit on your
ambition. It is the reason your ambition
matters.
And we in the government are doing our
part, fast and for real. Let me go
through very briefly. First, we are
doubling Germany's data center capacity
And with AI capacity growing fourfold.
And we are building a sovereign cloud
infrastructure for the state with
German-led consortia and young companies
along along side. We are the digital
wallet to market with more than 200
companies right now building
applications and solutions on it in an
open sandbox.
And third, the state becomes your first
customer, not just your regulator. In
our agentic AI hub, young companies,
more than 600, work directly with the
administration. So, come and help us
build the digital state.
We are connecting startups with a
Mittelstand
on sovereign infrastructure, so real
solutions get built here and stay here.
And we back also frontier model
development directly, including as an
anchor customer, because at the very
frontier, Europe still has ground to
make up, and we intend we're committed
to help close it.
And we are also clearing the path, less
bureaucracy, more freedom with a hard
commitment to cut reporting obligations
by 30% and to make a start and make
starting a company digital, standardized
and done within 48 hours. And the first
version will go live end of August. Are
we fast enough? Honestly, not yet.
But the rate of change is rising, and
that is what counts. We are moving in
the right direction, and above all, we
are building momentum also when you
don't feel it every day.
So, here is my invitation. Governments
can set direction, remove barriers, and
invest.
But the future in this room
will not be built by politics. It will
be built by you.
The developers, the founders, the ones
who are brave enough to try, to fail,
and to try again.
There has never been a better time to be
bold and to build.
We have purpose, so dream big, start
now, build it here. And when others tell
you it can't be done, that's the moment
to prove them wrong. We have what it
takes.
Let's build together. We are developers.
Thank you.
